Hi Samantha / Tom — great to meet you both. Thanks for the clear ask.

Recap of what we heard from the call:
- Targeted SLA: p99 < 500ms @ 4k context
- Burst to 200 qps (steady-state expected lower)
- Workload has high prefix reuse (conversational + templates)
- Procurement needs a 1M-token/month baseline TCO

What I'll attach: 1) a short PDF overview comparing Redwood vs two common hyperscaler endpoint setups (we include assumptions), and 2) an editable spreadsheet with the per-1M token model + knobs for batching, cache hit rate, and quantization.

Quick highlights (summary view):
- Redwood (recommended config: quantized int8, prefix caching enabled, moderate batching): ~ $6.2 per 1M generated tokens (includes compute amortized + infra + networking in our hosted pricing example).
- Hyperscaler A (managed endpoints, no prefix caching): ~ $18–22 per 1M tokens for similar model sizes when factoring per-host metered time + infra overhead.
- Hyperscaler B (serverless endpoints): ~ $12–16 per 1M tokens but with higher variance on p99 due to cold starts and scaling inefficiency.

Key levers that change cost: batching and cache hit rate. With a 35% prefix cache hit rate and 1.5x effective batching, Redwood model above drops to ~ $4.3 per 1M tokens in the same workload. We'll show the formulas in the spreadsheet.

Next tests I recommend:
1) Redwood-run 24h workload replay of a representative 10k request sample (you can provide or we can replay via Synapse) to measure real p99 and measured cache hit rate.
2) Comparative run against Hyperscaler A (we can help script the same load) to capture p99 and per-token cost under equivalent instance types.
3) A small canary with your traffic (1–2% of traffic) for 2 weeks to validate regression risk and cache behavior.

I've attached the PDF and the TCO spreadsheet. Aditya / Laura — can you confirm the backend assumptions in the attached spreadsheet (cost per GPU-hour, amortization, and network egress) and add a recommended quantization/instance mapping for the 4k context target?

Thanks — will set up a short follow-up call early next week to review the numbers with procurement.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 4, 2026 at 6:05 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached the PDF and the TCO spreadsheet. Aditya / Laura — can you confirm the backend assumptions...

Quick notes on the assumptions we used in the spreadsheet (confirming values):
- Model footprint: 13B-class (compatible with int8 quantization). Context length: 4k.
- Instance mix (Redwood hosted example): 1x dedciated GPU pod equivalency per sustained 150 qps at 4k (this is conservative for p99 SLAs). Effective cost = GPU-hour rate * utilization factor.
- GPU-hour rate assumption (public-equivalent): $2.50–$3.25/hr (we use blended $2.90/hr after reserved/spot mix for Dedicated customers).
- Token-generation throughput and batching: with continuous batching and 1.5x effective batching (typical with 10–50 qps bursts) we assume ~25% fewer GPU-hours vs naive per-request execution.
- Cache impact: prefix (KV) cache hit rates for this customer profile: 25–40% observed in similar customers. For modeling we use baseline 35% hit rate. Cache hit avoids repeated forward passes for the prefix, reducing total token compute by roughly the hit fraction. Effective per-1M token cost reduction ~= hit_rate * (prefix_length / avg_response_length) — spreadsheet has the exact line items.

Concrete numbers used in the sheet (rounded):
- Redwood baseline: $6.2 per 1M tokens (int8 + 35% cache hit + batching)
- Redwood no-cache/no-batching: $9.4 per 1M tokens
- Hyperscaler A (managed endpoint): $19.7 per 1M tokens (similar model, on-demand pricing, no prefix cache)
- Hyperscaler B (serverless): $13.5 per 1M tokens (variable p99 risk)

Risk & notes:
- Hyperscalers typically charge for the full instance-hour for warm endpoints; poor batching means wasted vCPU/GPU time.
- If Aurelia needs stricter p99 (<250ms) at 4k, cost delta narrows because both Redwood and hyperscalers require larger instance tiers; we should run the p99-focused test case.

Action for engineering: Jordan, can you prepare the 24h replay harness and instrument cache hit metrics + token breakdown (prefix vs generation) so we can feed real numbers into the sheet? Aditya, can you double-check the GPU-hour blend and network egress assumptions? I'll update the spreadsheet lines after you confirm.

—Laura
